articles.title: NRI Bride’s Murder Shocks Punjab: UK Fiancé Accused of Masterminding Gruesome Plot
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: The murder of 71-year-old NRI woman Rupinder Kaur Pandher in Ludhiana has emerged as one of the most shocking cases of 2025, exposing an elaborate plot allegedly orchestrated by her fiancé, Charanjit Singh Grewal, a 75-year-old UK-based NRI.

body.html:
The murder of 71-year-old NRI woman Rupinder Kaur Pandher in Ludhiana has emerged as one of the most shocking cases of 2025, exposing an elaborate plot allegedly orchestrated by her fiancé, Charanjit Singh Grewal, a 75-year-old UK-based NRI.

Rupinder, originally from Seattle, US, arrived in Ludhiana in July 2025 to marry Grewal, whom she had met through a matrimonial site. However, disputes over property and finances soon surfaced.

She began staying with Sukhjeet Singh alias Sonu, a local court typist who had known Grewal for over a decade. According to police, Grewal allegedly offered Sukhjeet ₹50 lakh and the promise of a new life abroad to carry out the killing.

On 12 July, at his home in Kila Raipur village, Sukhjeet murdered Rupinder with a baseball bat. He then burned her body, stuffed the remains into gunny sacks, and dumped them in a drain near Ghungrana or Lehra village in a bid to destroy evidence.

Police cracked the case after recovering skeletal remains, a burnt iPhone, and tools used in the crime. Sukhjeet, who even filed a false missing-persons report claiming Rupinder had travelled to Canada, later confessed during interrogation.

Investigators revealed that Rupinder had transferred significant sums to Grewal before travelling to India. The alleged motive was to prevent her from pursuing legal action against Grewal, who had backed out of the marriage.

Rupinder’s sister, Kamal Kaur Khairah, raised the alarm after losing contact with her, leading to intervention by the US embassy and Ludhiana police.

Currently, Sukhjeet Singh is in custody, while Grewal remains in the UK as the prime accused. Indian authorities have initiated diplomatic and legal steps to pursue him. Forensic teams continue to examine the recovered remains, while financial transactions are under scrutiny.

The case has attracted widespread national and international attention due to its cross-border links and gruesome execution.

articles.title: Meerut Shocker: Newlywed Couple’s Street Fight Turns into Viral Spectacle Outside Court!
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Meerut witnessed a dramatic altercation on Monday afternoon when a newlywed couple clashed publicly outside the courthouse near the Civil Lines police station.

body.html:
Meerut witnessed a dramatic altercation on Monday afternoon when a newlywed couple clashed publicly outside the courthouse near the Civil Lines police station.

Eyewitnesses captured the high-voltage drama on their mobile phones, showing the wife repeatedly assaulting her husband in the middle of the road. In the viral video, the woman can be seen grabbing her husband by the collar and throat, slapping him multiple times, and even biting his hand as stunned bystanders looked on.

Police said the couple, identified as Ishu from the Medical Police Station area and Dinesh from Partapur, Delhi Road, had married barely four months ago. However, their relationship soured soon after, with both parties filing cases against each other.

Reports claim Dinesh allegedly demanded dowry and threw Ishu out of the house within a week of marriage. Ishu has also accused him of instigating his brother to attempt rape. On the other hand, Dinesh has told police that his wife is having an extra-marital affair.

The clash broke out when the two encountered each other at the court premises. Witnesses said Ishu even climbed onto the bonnet of Dinesh’s car in a desperate attempt to stop him. When he finally halted, the heated confrontation unfolded right outside the Meerut Development Authority office.

Civil Line police intervened and took both into custody. Ishu was medically examined, and injuries were found on her body. Based on her complaint, police have registered an assault case against Dinesh. The viral video has now sparked intense discussion on social media.

articles.title: Jaipur Horror: Son Beats Mother to Death Over Gas Cylinder, Wi-Fi Row — Video Goes Viral
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking incident from Kardhani, Jaipur has surfaced, where Naveen Singh (31) brutally assaulted his mother, Santosh Devi (51), leading to her death.

body.html:
A shocking incident from Kardhani, Jaipur has surfaced, where Naveen Singh (31) brutally assaulted his mother, Santosh Devi (51), leading to her death.

The dispute reportedly began when Santosh Devi asked Naveen to replace an empty gas cylinder, which escalated after an argument over the Wi-Fi connection. In a viral video, Naveen is seen striking his mother with a stick while his father, Laxman Singh (a Delhi Police constable), and sister tried in vain to stop him.

Santosh Devi was rushed to the hospital but succumbed to 12 severe injuries, including fatal head wounds.

Police arrested Naveen on Tuesday. His father demanded the death penalty, saying: “He took the life of the mother who gave birth to him and destroyed our family.”

Investigations revealed Naveen had a history of drug abuse, unemployment, and violent behaviour. His wife left him in 2019, filing a dowry case in Bulandshahr, and a warrant was already issued against him.

The family was preparing for the daughter’s wedding in February 2026, which has now been shattered by the tragedy.

(The incident happened around 2 PM on Monday 15 September 2025 in Arun Vihar Colony. )

articles.title: Indore Student Dies After Consuming Poison, Setting Herself Ablaze; Family Accuses Boyfriend
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Indore: A 21-year-old student, Kriti, from Malharganj, died on Saturday evening after a shocking suicide attempt. She had allegedly been under prolonged harassment by her boyfriend, identified as Harsh Pandey, which pushed her into depression.

body.html:
Indore: A 21-year-old student, Kriti, from Malharganj, died on Saturday evening after a shocking suicide attempt. She had allegedly been under prolonged harassment by her boyfriend, identified as Harsh Pandey, which pushed her into depression.

On Friday, Kriti consumed poison and set herself on fire at her residence. Neighbours rushed her to Bathija Hospital on Airport Road, but despite treatment, she succumbed to injuries the next day.

Police said Kriti had previously tried to harm herself with a blade, knife, and even by opening the gas knob before taking the extreme step. In hospital, she reportedly cried about Harsh’s betrayal.

Her father, Mangesh Soni, alleged that Harsh exploited his daughter and refused marriage. “She was under treatment for depression since February due to his harassment,” he said. The family also claimed Harsh’s friends threatened them at the hospital to remain silent.

Harsh, originally from Bihar, studied with Kriti at IIM Indore. His father owns a medicine factory in Himachal Pradesh. Police confirmed a suicide note was recovered and said a case is being registered based on the family’s statements.

Kriti’s tragic death has sparked outrage, with her family demanding strict action against the accused.

articles.title: Assam Civil Service Officer Held with ₹1.7 Cr Cash & Jewellery in Vigilance Raid
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Guwahati: The Chief Minister’s Special Vigilance Cell on Monday arrested ACS officer Nupur Bora for allegedly amassing disproportionate assets. Raids at her Guwahati residence in Shine Shanti Greeno led to the recovery of ₹92 lakh in cash and jewellery worth nearly ₹1 crore.

body.html:
Guwahati: The Chief Minister’s Special Vigilance Cell on Monday arrested ACS officer Nupur Bora for allegedly amassing disproportionate assets.

Raids at her Guwahati residence in Shine Shanti Greeno led to the recovery of ₹92 lakh in cash and jewellery worth nearly ₹1 crore. Another ₹10 lakh was seized from her rented house in Barpeta. In total, assets worth ₹1.7 crore were uncovered.

Bora, a 2019 batch officer from Golaghat, was serving as Circle Officer in Goroimari (Kamrup). CM Himanta Biswa Sarma said she was under watch for six months following complaints of land-transfer scams. “She had transferred Hindu land to suspicious individuals for money while posted in Barpeta,” he alleged, adding that corruption in revenue circles of minority-dominated areas was rampant.

The Vigilance Cell also raided the residence of her alleged aide, Lat Mandal Surajit Deka, accused of acquiring multiple land properties in Barpeta in collusion with Bora.

Authorities are now scrutinising seized cash, documents, and her past tenure as ADC in Karbi Anglong, where she was already facing questions over irregularities.
